intro.title: conic-gradient
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a colorful pie chart using CSS conic gradients. You will learn how to create smooth color transitions around a circle, starting from a single point. The core concept is the conic-gradient() function, which allows you to define colors at specific angles. You will work with CSS properties like background-image and border-radius to style your chart. By the end, you'll be able to create radial color patterns for visual elements on a webpage.
intro.usecase: Conic gradients are commonly used in modern UI design to create circular progress indicators, pie charts, and color wheels in dashboards and data visualization tools. You'll see them in fitness apps showing activity rings, financial apps displaying budget allocations, or analytics platforms visualizing percentage distributions. Developers implement conic gradients for loading spinners, rating displays, and circular menus that require smooth color transitions around a center point. This technique is essential for creating visually engaging circular interfaces without complex image assets.
